Does the balance a company closed on reopen in the next filing?

Source: R/check_continuity.R
check_continuity.Rd

Every other check in this package reads one annual report and asks whether it agrees with itself. This one compares filings: the balance sheet a company closed on at the end of one year is the balance it opens on in the next, and the two figures are filed a year apart.

Usage

check_continuity(x, by = "cvr", filing = "year", tol = 1, rel = 0.001)

Arguments

x

Facts from several filings, with elementid, value, the columns named by by and filing, and instant – plus startdate and enddate if the income statement is to be compared as well.

by

Column identifying the company. Default "cvr".

filing

Column identifying the filing, used to order the two statements. Default "year"; a table from read_xbrl() carries period_end instead, so pass that.

tol

Absolute tolerance in the reporting currency. Default 1.

rel

Relative tolerance below which a difference is called rounding. Default 0.001.

Value

A tibble with one row per figure stated twice: the by column, elementid, period (the instant, or the span a duration covers), the two filings and their values, diff, rel, and verdict – "agrees", "rounding", "scaled" where the ratio is a power of a thousand, or "differs".

The one check a single filing cannot make

A filing scaled wrongly all the way through is internally perfect. Its balance balances, its cascade reconciles, every structural test in this package passes – because everything in it was multiplied by the same number. Only a figure from outside disagrees.

Across 4,304 Danish filings this found 84 such figures, 8 out by a thousand and 76 by a thousandth. Nothing else here would have seen them.

A difference is not always an error

Companies restate. Where more than half a balance sheet's lines disagree the filer has changed something deliberately – a change of accounting policy, a correction, a merger – and a statistic needs to know that rather than treat it as noise. Where one line moves and the rest hold, it is a correction to that line. The verdicts say which shape it is; neither is called wrong.

What is compared

Undimensioned figures, where two filings state the same element for the same date – a balance by its instant, an income statement line by the period it covers. Both are things a company says twice: the comparative column of one filing against the primary column of the one before it.

Comparatives inside a single filing are not used. They are the same document making the same claim twice, and agreeing with itself proves nothing.

See also

check_movement(), which checks the same balance through one year rather than across two.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# every filing of every company in one table
x  <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")
cc <- check_continuity(x, filing = "period_end")

cc[cc$verdict == "scaled", ]     # a filing multiplied all the way through
} # }
